scenes.situation: A traveler walks up to you on the road.
scenes.grammar: 你好 is the everyday hello. Answering 你好 with 你好 is completely normal.
scenes.note: 你好 means hello, so you greet them back with 你好. 再见 is goodbye and 谢谢 is thank you.

scenes.situation: The traveler packs up and gets ready to leave.
scenes.grammar: 再见 literally means “see again”: it is the usual way to say goodbye.
scenes.note: 再见 means goodbye, so you say 再见 back. 你好 is hello and 谢谢 is thank you.
scenes.result: The traveler waves and heads down the road.

scenes.situation: You trip and spill the traveler’s water. What do you say?
scenes.note: 对不起 means sorry: use it when you have caused a problem. 谢谢 is thank you and 你好 is hello.
scenes.result: The traveler laughs it off and refills the flask.

scenes.grammar: 我 means “I”. 要 expresses wanting something here. The traveler is telling you what they would like.
scenes.note: 茶 names tea leaves here. Water and tea leaves make the drink.
scenes.result: You prepare tea with the leaves and water.

scenes.py: Wǒ yào mǐfàn. Wǒ yào cài.
scenes.en: I would like rice. I would like some dishes.
scenes.grammar: 我 means “I”. 要 expresses wanting something here. The traveler is telling you what they would like.
scenes.note: 米饭 is cooked rice. 菜 here means prepared dishes; our tray contains vegetables.
scenes.result: You serve the cooked rice and vegetable side dish.
